newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani unions condemn journalist court martial.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani unions condemn journalist court martial.

text.p: Pakistan's newspaper unions on Thursday condemned the reported secret court martial of a journalist detained by security forces for more than a month on unspecified charges.

A joint statement by the Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists and the All-Pakistan Newspaper Employees Confederation called the detention of Humayun Far illegal and said his trial by a military court would "set a very dangerous precedent with far-reaching implications".
Far, Islamabad bureau chief of the Urdu-language daily Mashriq, was detained near his home on June 28 and has been held incommunicado.

His lawyers said on Monday they had been told during secret proceedings of a civilian court hearing their petition against his disappearance that Far was already facing a court martial under a military law.
Attorney General Chaudhary Farooq Ahmed had asked for the hearing by the Lahore High Court to be in camera because of the seriousness of the charges that he said were linked with Pakistan's security.
Thursday's statement by the unions said the court martial "a violation of fundamental rights" and Far should tried in an open court and allowed the facility of release on bail and engaging a counsel.
